item.title: [6.7] RouteWeaver: Weaving Mode Selection and Execution into Unified LLM Routing
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

LLM routing dynamically selects and coordinates heterogeneous language models across diverse tasks. However, existing approaches are largely built around a predefined execution paradigm, such as single-round, multi-round, or agentic routing, which fixes how model calls are organized and limits adaptation to different query needs. We propose RouteWeaver, a unified routing framework that...

WHY IT MATTERS

RouteWeaver introduces a unified LLM routing framework that jointly optimizes mode selection and execution using a novel training approach, addressing a clear limitation in current heterogeneous model orchestration.

item.title: [6.4] Heartbeat Thinking: Speculative Reasoning and Tool Execution While Listening in Realtime Voice Agents
item.description:
WHAT HAPPENED

Tool-using voice agents often leave users waiting after speech ends, even when actionable information arrives earlier in the request. Speculative approaches begin work during speech, but chunk-bounded or interrupt-on-update generation can truncate a tool call before its arguments are complete. This couples computation time to speech updates, limiting useful work completed in advance.

WHY IT MATTERS

item.description:

Robots must act under physical and social constraints while adapting to changes in their environment and human needs. Existing embodied-agent systems often focus on specified goals or abstract execution into symbolic actions, limiting evaluation in an evolving world. We introduce TARSphere, a robot-oriented full-stack framework for physically and socially grounded long-horizon embodied agents.
